  WHY: Reviewers disagreed on severity (NIT vs MAJOR), but the highest reported severity is MAJOR; the disabled-gate path still changes the payload shape and can mislead downstream consumers.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:640-660 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: normalize_diagnose_result_contract_fields() lacks robust error handling around missing/unreadable input, temp-file creation, and jq I/O failures, so normalization can corrupt or mask diagnose output.
  WHY: Both reviewers described file/IO failure modes that can overwrite the result path with partial/empty JSON or turn a valid diagnose run into a fallback.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:708-715 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The trace-contract check is advisory-only; when Codex output fails it, the script leaves `DIAGNOSE_SUCCESS` false and still routes to fallback instead of forcing failure or marking the run unhandled.
  WHY: The warning only appears in logs, so the primary LLM path can be bypassed while callers still treat the run as successfully handled.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:720-750 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The deterministic no-JSON fallback result omits top-level `evidence_trace` and `hypothesis` fields.
  WHY: The fallback body builds trace text in shell variables, but the jq-built result JSON does not carry those contract fields through, violating the extended output schema.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:389-399,424-438 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The static-prefix and prompt-template fallback paths still produce pre-Phase-D output or only embed trace data in body text, without guaranteeing top-level `evidence_trace` and `hypothesis`.
  WHY: Those fallback templates remain contract-incomplete on the paths Grok identified, so a no-JSON/invalid-JSON run can still emit output missing the new required fields.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 688-700, the `format_diagnose_trace_section` function, specifically line 695: `+ (.observation // "No observation provided.")`
  Problem: The jq `//` operator treats empty string as truthy, so when a model returns `"observation": ""`, the fallback `"No observation provided."` does not activate.
  Why it fails at runtime: A diagnose run that produces valid JSON with an empty-string observation will have its trace section rendered with visually malformed lines, degrading debuggability.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh
  Line or code reference: Lines 654-668, the `normalize_diagnose_result_contract_fields` function
  Problem: This function unconditionally adds `evidence_trace: []` and `hypothesis: ""` to every result it touches, even when `DIAGNOSE_TRACE_REQUIRED` is disabled.
  Why it fails at runtime: If an operator ever sets `DIAGNOSE_TRACE_REQUIRED=false`, the emitted diagnose JSON will still include `evidence_trace` and `hypothesis` fields, violating the contract that says these fields are optional when the gate is off.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  Why it fails at runtime: Disk-full or permission errors cause normalization to fail, causing the caller to fall back despite otherwise-valid Codex output, violating service uptime by unnecessary recovery workflows.
